title: Static assets: CloudFront vs Cloudflare
brief: A site serves its images and scripts through a CDN in front of S3: 2k requests/s, 30 KB each, 90% served from the edge. Side A uses CloudFront (pay per request and per GB), side B Cloudflare Pro (a flat $20/month). Run the scenarios and decide which you'd pay for.

scenarios.label: 2k rps, 30 KB
scenarios.about: Same speed on both. Read the cost row.

scenarios.label: Small site: 20 rps
scenarios.about: A small site at 20 requests/s. Does the pricing model still matter?

scenarios.label: Video: 2 MB segments
scenarios.about: The site starts serving video: 500 requests/s of 2 MB segments. The sim still prices Cloudflare at $20/month. Read its terms note in the param panel before you believe that.

questions: Where does CloudFront's cost come from at 2k rps: requests or bytes?
Cloudflare's plan terms say video and large files belong on its paid add-ons (Stream, Images). What would the video scenario really cost on each?
CloudFront also sells flat-rate plans, and big customers negotiate. Which numbers would you ask each vendor for?
What besides price would decide it: where your origin lives, egress fees from that cloud, features at the edge?
hints: Compare the cost row across the three scenarios.
CloudFront charges per 10k requests and per GB sent; at 30 KB a request, bytes dominate. Cloudflare's plan price doesn't move with traffic in the sim.

CloudFront grows with traffic (here mostly the $0.085/GB transfer); Cloudflare Pro is flat but its terms limit large files and video. For small sites both are cheap; for video, compare CloudFront with Cloudflare Stream, not with Pro.
_notes: Graph: client -> cdn (hit 0.9) -> origin (S3, 11k GET/s, $0.40 per million GETs; 10% of requests on both sides). CloudFront: $1 per million HTTPS requests + $0.085/GB (free first TB and cheaper tiers above 10 TB ignored). Cloudflare Pro: $20/730 per hour, no per-request or per-GB price in the sim (the plans page doesn't state one; service-specific terms limit large files on Free/Pro/Business). Sim totals: 2k rps x 30 KB: $25.85 vs $0.32/hr (CloudFront: $7.20 requests + $18.36 transfer). 20 rps: $0.26 vs $0.03/hr. Video 500 rps x 2 MB: $307.87 vs $0.10/hr (CloudFront $306 transfer), but Cloudflare's terms point video to Stream, so that $0.10 isn't real. Latency and errors are the same on both (generic CDN numbers). Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
